messages.content:
You are the investigation agent of Bianque. Bianque investigates Kubernetes alerts from read-only evidence and writes a report in which every conclusion cites evidence.

Evidence discipline:

1. Every statement of fact cites the IDs of the evidence it rests on (`ev_` followed by ten hexadecimal digits). Cite only IDs that appear in the evidence you were given.
2. When the evidence does not establish a root cause, say that the root cause is unknown. Do not guess.
3. Knowledge (`kn_` IDs, from runbooks) is not evidence. It may only be listed as a reference, never cited for a fact.
4. You never change the system. A command that changes something (for example a kubectl write verb, a helm upgrade or a git push) may only appear in a remediation suggestion of risk `change`, for a person to confirm.

Your task: write the report of this investigation from the evidence below.

- Summary and impact: what happened and what it affects, in plain sentences.
- Timeline: the events of the incident in time order, each citing evidence. The alert itself is evidence.
- Root cause: identified only when the cited evidence shows it. Give its category, the Kubernetes object it is in (kind, namespace, name, and the field when known), one statement, the citations and your confidence. When the evidence does not establish a root cause, set the status to unknown, cite nothing and set the confidence to low.
- Claims: the other definite statements the report makes, each citing evidence.
- Missing evidence: every failed call listed below, and any other evidence you would have needed, with the reason it is missing. A failed call of the logs domain rules out a high confidence.
- Suggestions: remediations for a person to confirm. Mark each `read_only` or `change`; a command that changes something is always `change`. Each cites the evidence that motivates it.
- References: the knowledge you relied on, by knowledge ID and title. Never cite knowledge as evidence.
- Follow-up questions: questions a reader may want to ask next.

tool_calls.arguments: {"schema_version": "1", "summary": "A Deployment rollout in namespace demo-s1 changed the APP_MODE environment variable of the s1-app container from \"standard\" to \"invalid\". The application rejects this value at startup, logs an error, and exits with code 2, causing the new pod (s1-app-5468546b65-gjkcl) to enter CrashLoopBackOff and never become Ready.", "impact": "The s1-app Deployment is stuck mid-rollout: revision 2's pod is in CrashLoopBackOff and not Ready, so the application is unavailable (readiness probe fails with connection refused). The Deployment reports unavailable=1 and the Progressing condition shows the new ReplicaSet is still progressing.", "timeline": [{"time": "2026-10-19T22:40:36Z", "event": "Initial manifests added (commit 4f0fae5a6665) and revision 1 ReplicaSet s1-app-666f75b99 created with APP_MODE=standard; pod s1-app-666f75b99-9q7v7 scheduled and started.", "citations": ["ev_944b966441", "ev_147f2d80d2", "ev_25b03cf7e5"]}, {"time": "2026-10-19T22:40:43Z", "event": "Commit 617e33d62ee7 'Update app mode configuration' changes APP_MODE from 'standard' to 'invalid' in deployment.yaml.", "citations": ["ev_bebbdb4ced", "ev_944b966441"]}, {"time": "2026-10-19T22:40:44Z", "event": "Revision 2 ReplicaSet s1-app-5468546b65 created (APP_MODE=invalid); pod s1-app-5468546b65-gjkcl scheduled.", "citations": ["ev_147f2d80d2", "ev_25b03cf7e5"]}, {"time": "2026-10-19T22:41:25Z", "event": "Container app starts and immediately exits with error 'invalid APP_MODE \"invalid\"; expected one of: readonly, standard' (exit code 2).", "citations": ["ev_22f8434e8b", "ev_ff96737437"]}, {"time": "2026-10-19T22:41:25Z", "event": "Readiness probe fails (connection refused) as the container is not serving.", "citations": ["ev_25b03cf7e5", "ev_6d6000f56e"]}, {"time": "2026-10-19T22:41:29Z", "event": "BackOff event: back-off restarting failed container app (count 8).", "citations": ["ev_25b03cf7e5", "ev_6d6000f56e"]}, {"time": "2026-10-19T22:41:42Z", "event": "Alert BianquePodRestarting fires for pod s1-app-5468546b65-gjkcl.", "citations": ["ev_fcab18dda7"]}], "root_cause": {"status": "identified", "category": "config_error", "object": {"kind": "Deployment", "namespace": "demo-s1", "name": "s1-app", "field": "spec.template.spec.containers[app].env[APP_MODE]"}, "statement": "The APP_MODE environment variable was set to the invalid value 'invalid' (valid values are 'readonly' and 'standard'), causing the app container to exit with code 2 and enter CrashLoopBackOff.", "citations": ["ev_bebbdb4ced", "ev_147f2d80d2", "ev_67fd6463e6", "ev_22f8434e8b", "ev_ff96737437"], "confidence": "high"}, "claims": [{"statement": "The app container rejects APP_MODE='invalid' and exits with code 2, logging 'ERROR invalid APP_MODE \"invalid\"; expected one of: readonly, standard'.", "citations": ["ev_22f8434e8b", "ev_ff96737437"]}, {"statement": "The invalid value was introduced by commit 617e33d62ee7, which changed APP_MODE from 'standard' to 'invalid'.", "citations": ["ev_bebbdb4ced"]}, {"statement": "Revision 2 (ReplicaSet s1-app-5468546b65) carries APP_MODE=invalid, while revision 1 (s1-app-666f75b99) carried APP_MODE=standard.", "citations": ["ev_147f2d80d2", "ev_67fd6463e6"]}, {"statement": "The pod s1-app-5468546b65-gjkcl has restart_count 3 and is in CrashLoopBackOff (waiting).", "citations": ["ev_ff96737437"]}, {"statement": "The image pull is not the cause: no ImagePullBackOff/ErrImagePull events exist and the image was already present on the machine.", "citations": ["ev_6d6000f56e", "ev_25b03cf7e5"]}, {"statement": "The readiness probe fails with connection refused because the container is not running/serving.", "citations": ["ev_25b03cf7e5", "ev_6d6000f56e"]}], "missing_evidence": [{"what": "Current (non-previous) container logs for the app container", "reason": "Only the previous attempt's log was retrieved; the current attempt's log would further confirm the same startup error but is not strictly required given the previous log and termination state."}], "suggestions": [{"action": "Revert the APP_MODE environment variable from 'invalid' back to 'standard' (or a valid value) in the Deployment s1-app in namespace demo-s1.", "risk": "change", "command": "kubectl -n demo-s1 set env deployment/s1-app APP_MODE=standard", "citations": ["ev_bebbdb4ced", "ev_67fd6463e6", "ev_22f8434e8b"]}, {"action": "Revert commit 617e33d62ee7 in the manifest repository to restore APP_MODE=standard.", "risk": "change", "command": "git revert 617e33d62ee7", "citations": ["ev_bebbdb4ced", "ev_944b966441"]}, {"action": "Add validation (e.g. a CI check or admission policy) to reject APP_MODE values outside the allowed set {readonly, standard}.", "risk": "change", "citations": ["ev_22f8434e8b"]}], "references": [{"knowledge_id": "kn_b728d580f575", "title": "CrashLoopBackOff > What CrashLoopBackOff means"}, {"knowledge_id": "kn_c73d8439117f", "title": "CrashLoopBackOff > Reading the previous container log"}, {"knowledge_id": "kn_fa369be3768e", "title": "CrashLoopBackOff > Collecting the termination state"}, {"knowledge_id": "kn_255795fa4d69", "title": "CrashLoopBackOff > Restart backoff timing"}], "followup_questions": ["Who authored and approved commit 617e33d62ee7 that set APP_MODE=invalid?", "Why was the value 'invalid' chosen, and is there a valid intended value (readonly vs standard)?", "Should the application fail fast on an invalid APP_MODE, or should it default to a safe value?", "Is there a rollback policy or canary gate that should have prevented this rollout from proceeding?"]}
